title: When the Ember Wakes Revisited
premise: Yara Ishikawa, once a battle-mage sworn to the ember-god Vessia, has hidden her gift for three years in Greyhollow, a city where magic is outlawed and her god has gone silent. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone with the gift, Yara's small charms draw suspicion, and she flees into the wilds with a hunted child-mage named Oren and a disgraced hunter, Captain Dain Ferro, who once served the same covenant. Together they discover that Vessia did not die—she was imprisoned by the other realms' gods, who fear that her fire could unmake the long winter they imposed to punish humanity. To free her, Yara must gather three ember-shards scattered across hostile territories, reforge the broken covenant between gods and mortals, and accept that justice outside the law may cost her everything. In the end, Yara sacrifices her own memories of the people she loves to reignite Vessia, ending the winter but waking to strangers who remember her only as a legend.
about_author: X. M. Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trial records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about faith, survival, and the people history forgets, and live somewhere cold with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Yara sells a luck-charm to a desperate dockworker in Greyhollow, hiding her gift behind mundane craft. POV: Yara. The emotional beat is quiet dread—she has made invisibility an art, but the arrival of crown proclamations promising gold for reporting mages makes her small life feel like a lit fuse.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: A neighbor denounces Yara; witch-hunters raid her shop while she escapes through the cellar with nothing but her old covenant-sigil. POV: Yara. The beat is loss and rage—the city she served as a mercenary discards her overnight, and she realizes staying invisible was always an illusion.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Burned Bright
chapters.summary: Fleeing the walls, Yara finds Oren, a ten-year-old whose magic flares when he cries, hunted after his village burned. POV: Yara. The beat is reluctant tenderness; protecting him forces her to use forbidden power openly for the first time in years, and Vessia's silence begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Confession
chapters.summary: Captain Dain Ferro corners them on the frost-road but cannot strike—he recognizes Yara's sigil from the war he helped lose. POV: Dain. The beat is shame and defection; he reveals the hunt is cover for the crown seizing mage-blood for rituals, and chooses exile beside the people he was sent to catch.

chapters.title: Shard of the First Flame
chapters.summary: In the drowned temple of Ashfall, the trio retrieves the first ember-shard, guarded by a wraith of Yara's dead comrades. POV: Yara. The beat is grief confronted; the wraith accuses her of surviving when her sworn brothers died holding the line, and she answers honestly for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Winter Remembers
chapters.summary: Crossing the frozen pass, Oren nearly dies of cold-touched sickness, and Yara bargains with a river-god for aid, learning the other realms' gods imprisoned Vessia out of fear. POV: Oren. The beat is wonder and terror through a child's eyes—the divine world is real, vast, and hostile to mortals who ask questions.

chapters.title: The Court of Quiet Gods
chapters.summary: Dain's former order captures them; at trial, Yara speaks truth about the winter's origin instead of pleading innocence, splitting the hunters against their own commanders. POV: Dain. The beat is moral courage; some hunters defect, others turn violent, and the trio escapes in blood toward the second shard.

chapters.title: Two Shards, One Price
chapters.summary: Yara claims the second shard from a mountain shrine by surrendering her happiest memory—her mother's face—as payment. POV: Yara. The beat is sacrifice made tangible; she feels herself hollowing and hides it from Oren, understanding now what reforging the covenant will truly cost.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: At the prison-peak where Vessia sleeps, the third shard lies in the hands of the winter-god Halveth himself. Yara challenges him, Oren's raw gift shatters the god's anchor, and Dain holds the pass alone against the crown's army. POV: rotating. The climax: Yara drives the shards into Vessia's heart and offers all her remaining memories as kindling.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: The winter breaks; spring floods Greyhollow's streets. Yara wakes with no past, tended by Oren—who refuses to let her vanish—and Dain, who tells her stories until some warmth returns. POV: Yara. The resolution: justice came outside any law, survival had its price, and love, not memory, becomes the covenant's new foundation.
